oracle.why: The oracles below are micromark extensions, which emit a token stream rather than a tree. remark is the harness that runs them and turns the tokens into mdast, so it is what this gate executes — but the syntax decisions being compared are the extensions' own.

authorities.directives: micromark-extension-directive@4.0.0 for directive envelopes, labels, and attachment positions (run through remark-directive); the shared attribute member grammar is explicitly Pandoc-owned

oracle.astShapeFrom: mdast-util-directive@3.1.0 and mdast-util-from-markdown; every `ast-shape` delta below originates here, not in the parser extensions.
oracle.note: Versions are pinned by pnpm-lock.yaml. This is a corrective and supplementary oracle: cmark remains the CommonMark oracle and cmark-gfm the GFM-extension oracle, while remark/mdast supplies independent evidence for directives, math, footnote representation, tables, and the reference-link model.
notAnAuthorityFor: Which construct wins when two extensions could claim the same line. That is decided by micromark's construct priority and by this repository's audited extension attachment order — each an artifact of its own architecture, not a rule either project specifies. Divergences of that kind are product grammar decisions rather than mdast parity deltas.

LaTeX-style math delimiters. micromark-extension-math implements `$` and `$$` only, so `\(x\)` and `\[x\]` reach remark as ordinary escaped brackets. It has no opinion there to compare against, which is why packages/markdown-core/tests/fixtures/extensions-formula-latex.txt is deliberately absent from the corpus below rather than present with six registered divergences. Registering them would read as `remark disagrees`, and it does not — it was never asked.

Whether an extension is on. The dialect has no switches and every parse attaches every extension, so what an input parses to with a scanner excluded is not a property of the product; no fixture and no gate asserts it.

Attribute member grammar and consumer projection. Markdown Core deliberately uses the pinned Pandoc 3.11 grammar at every attachment site and projects IDs to the universal anchor and remaining values to shared classes and records; remark remains the evidence only for the directive envelope and attachment position, which the directives module states. New runtime differences caused by that planned migration must be registered when they begin reproducing.

claim: Within the evidence boundary above, Markdown Core's semantics are identical to the unified/remark ecosystem's except for the registered differences below. The check that enforces current runtime behavior is scripts/check-mdast-parity.mjs.

deltas.summary: mdast puts a text directive's label content directly in the directive's children. Markdown Core owns a dedicated DirectiveLabel node through the label field; it is markup, but is not a semantic child of the directive body.
deltas.handling: The comparison projects mdast's label children into the dedicated label field, so label content is compared without pretending it belongs to the directive's child sequence.

deltas.summary: mdast has no soft-break node; a soft line break is a newline inside a text value. Markdown Core makes it a SoftBreak node.
deltas.handling: The normalizer splits remark's text values on newlines.

deltas.summary: mdast distinguishes leafDirective from containerDirective. Markdown Core represents both as DirectiveBlock.
deltas.handling: Both remark kinds map to DirectiveBlock.

deltas.summary: A run consisting only of the spaces a break strips left an empty text node in cmark's model, which this repository inherited until 0a.14 (D12/D13); mdast has never had one, and as of 0a.14 neither does this side. The delta is now UPSTREAM-ONLY.
deltas.handling: Empty text is dropped from both sides before comparing. Current cmark and cmark-gfm can still produce one.
deltas.evidence: The fail-closed projections are registered independently in specs/oracles/cmark/deltas.json and specs/oracles/cmark-gfm/deltas.json.

deltas.summary: A line ending inside an inline code span is a space in this repository AST and stays a line ending in mdast.
deltas.authority: cmark. CommonMark states that a code span line ending is treated as a space; cmark applies it when it builds the node, and mdast-util-to-hast applies it at render time instead. The two agree on the span content; they disagree on which layer states it.
deltas.handling: The oracle converts line endings in mdast inline code before comparing, so the comparison is about the span content.
deltas.evidence: scripts/lib/mdast-oracle.mjs, inlineCode; the base-language claim is checked by scripts/check-upstream-parity.mjs over spec.txt.

deltas.summary: mdast keeps an HTML comment as an `html` node holding the token as written. Markdown Core makes it a `Comment` whose literal is the bytes between `<!--` and `-->`: the inline token, and a flow HTML node that opens with `<!--` and whose end line holds only whitespace after the first `-->`.
deltas.handling: The comparison maps mdast's comment nodes to `Comment` with the delimiters removed, the rule the engine applies on its own side (`docs/specs/dialect/comments.md`); cmark owns the token and block boundaries, and this projection only keeps the two models in one shape where a comment appears.

deltas.summary: mdast keeps a link reference definition as a `definition` node where it was written and leaves `linkReference` and `imageReference` unresolved, carrying the label. Markdown Core consumes the definition into the parser's map and resolves every successful reference into the `Link` or `Media` it names (M2), as cmark does.
deltas.handling: The comparison resolves mdast's references against its own definitions inside the projection -- the first definition of an identifier wins, as in both grammars -- into `Link`/`Media` carrying the definition's destination and title, drops the definition nodes, and leaves a reference with no definition as the prose both models make of it. The label bytes are compared through the resolved destination, so a reference that resolved to the wrong definition, or to none, still shows up as a difference.

deltas.summary: mdast retains ragged table rows. Markdown Core applies the delimiter column count while building its AST, as mdast-util-to-hast does when rendering: missing cells are empty and excess cells are omitted.
deltas.handling: The mdast projection uses each table's own alignment count to complete or truncate its rows and identify its header, including nested tables. The native tree is not normalized, so incorrect native row widths still fail comparison.
deltas.evidence: docs/specs/dialect/tables.md; syntax-tree/mdast-util-to-hast lib/handlers/table-row.js; the remark corpus covers short, long, and nested rows.

deltas.summary: mdast records blank separation on both a list and its items; Markdown Core stores one tight flag per list.
deltas.handling: A projected list is tight only when neither the list nor any direct item is spread. Nested lists are evaluated independently. Native tight flags are unchanged.
deltas.evidence: syntax-tree/mdast-util-to-hast lib/handlers/list-item.js listLoose; remark corpus nested task and loose item cases.

deltas.summary: Boolean-only oracles retain task completion but lose the authored marker spelling, including x versus X.
deltas.handling: Compare the three shared states: absent, incomplete and complete. Exact marker spelling remains covered by canonical fixtures and binding tests; the non-leading [x] witness still compares unequal completion states.

deltas.summary: The canonical table stores head/content/foot groups and positive cell spans; pipe tables have one head row and unit spans.
deltas.handling: The oracle projection groups its first row as TableHead, its remaining rows as TableBody, and adds an empty TableFoot; cells gain rowspan=1 and colspan=1. Native table topology and spans are compared unchanged.
deltas.evidence: docs/specs/dialect/tables.md; canonical table fixtures and existing pipe-table oracle corpus.

notDeltas.summary: Both keep every footnote definition, unreferenced ones included: remark at its source position, Markdown Core as a document-owned `Footnote` ordered by scope start, which the gate lifts into one order. This independently corrects cmark-gfm's extension-specific destructive placement model.
notDeltas.evidence: docs/specs/canonical-ast.md footnote semantics; verified on in-body, out-of-order, unreferenced, and dangling cases.

notDeltas.summary: Inline math strips one leading and one trailing space when both are present and the content is not all spaces, with line endings counting as spaces. Markdown Core did not do this until it was found by this oracle; it now matches.
notDeltas.evidence: micromark-extension-math states the rule; packages/markdown-core/tests/fixtures/extensions-formula-github.txt pins it.

notDeltas.summary: A footnote reference whose label no document footnote defines is literal text in both, label included and unparsed. This was a registered divergence until 2026-08-02, when Markdown Core adopted the rule the two oracles already shared; it is recorded here so the corpus keeps checking that the agreement holds.

expectedDivergences.summary: mdast carries an image's alternative text as a string property; this repository carries it as inline children.
expectedDivergences.why: Children keep the alt text's own inline structure addressable. Neither model can express the other's shape, so the comparison stops at the destination and title.

expectedDivergences.summary: A single-dollar span whose content is padded is not math here; remark-math accepts it.
expectedDivergences.why: GitHub's renderer is the evidence for `$...$`, and its heuristics exist to keep prose about money from becoming math. remark-math has no such heuristic.

expectedDivergences.summary: As above, with the padding on the closing side.

expectedDivergences.summary: Prose containing two dollar amounts is not math here; remark-math parses `$300B and ~$` as an expression.
expectedDivergences.why: This is the case GitHub's heuristics exist for, and the one that would make the extension unusable in ordinary prose.

expectedDivergences.summary: GitHub's `$`...`$` form delimits math with backticks; the content is `x+y`. remark-math does not implement the form and keeps the backticks in the value.
expectedDivergences.why: Documented at docs.github.com writing-mathematical-expressions as the form to use when the expression contains Markdown-conflicting characters.

expectedDivergences.summary: As above; remark-math additionally mis-terminates on the escaped dollar.

expectedDivergences.summary: `$$...$$` alone on a line is a block formula here; remark-math makes it inline math inside a paragraph.
